paragraphs: As of Thursday, October 8, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq is trying to stabilize after its first decline in six sessions. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.22% Wednesday to 27,538.69, just below Tuesday's record, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.22%. Treasury yields were the main obstacle: the 10-year briefly reached about 5.36% before retreating to 5.28% after a well-received auction, and the 30-year yield touched a 24-year high. Semiconductor participation was mixed, with Micron rising roughly 4% while Nvidia and TSMC declined. AI demand remains a supportive structural force, but the market is becoming more sensitive to financing costs and the breadth of chip leadership.

The Fed's September meeting minutes showed agreement on raising rates but disagreement over whether energy-related price risks or demand-driven inflation posed the larger threat. Another hike later this year remains possible, although futures pricing placed the probability of an October increase near 17%. Oil eased after the International Energy Agency agreed to accelerate planned reserve releases, with Brent settling near $100.20. Continuing shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz mean energy-driven inflation pressure could return quickly. The immediate Nasdaq question is whether resilient AI earnings can overcome the valuation pressure from high long-term yields.

catalysts.title: Fed Governor Waller — 4:30 AM ET; initial jobless claims — 8:30 AM ET
catalysts.detail: Waller's economic outlook and the weekly labor-market report will help determine whether investors continue expecting an October Fed pause. A steady labor picture with less hawkish policy commentary would support bonds; renewed inflation concern or stronger-than-expected labor could push long yields higher.

catalysts.title: U.S. 30-year Treasury auction — 1:00 PM ET
catalysts.detail: Demand for long-duration government debt is a critical test after the 30-year yield reached a 24-year high. Wednesday's well-received 10-year auction eased yields and equity losses. A weak 30-year sale could reverse that relief and pressure Nasdaq valuations.

catalysts.title: Oil supply and Strait of Hormuz shipping risks — ongoing
catalysts.detail: The IEA's acceleration of previously planned stock releases helped oil ease Wednesday, but shipping incidents continue to create supply uncertainty. Nasdaq is especially exposed if crude and long-term inflation expectations rise together.

catalysts.title: Applied Digital results and broader semiconductor follow-through — throughout the session
catalysts.detail: Applied Digital reported quarterly revenue of $341.9 million, up 322%, and an adjusted loss of one cent per share. Its large GAAP loss and substantial debt also underscore the cost of financing AI infrastructure. Watch whether the results support broader semiconductor and AI-infrastructure shares, not just individual winners.

catalysts.title: PepsiCo earnings — before the open
catalysts.detail: The report offers a read on consumer demand, pricing power and input costs. The most relevant market-wide signal is whether companies can preserve margins without adding inflation pressure or seeing demand weaken.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the positive scenario is contained oil, a patient Fed tone, stable labor data and solid demand at the afternoon bond auction, allowing SOX and other technology shares to regain broad leadership. The negative scenario is another simultaneous rise in crude and long yields while financing-sensitive AI infrastructure companies underperform. The market's response to strong corporate results will be an important test of whether technology momentum remains durable.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 AM ET. Key checkpoints are Waller's remarks at 4:30 AM ET, initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET and the 30-year Treasury auction at 1:00 PM ET. PepsiCo reports before the open; oil and semiconductor breadth remain live indicators.
